questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was incredibly difficult, and it was made harder by the fact, that the university without any warning only gave us 24 days to find accomodation or else we would not be allowed to come after all. I found something very bad right before the deadline, and when I arrived I moved to another location, which was much better and not that difficult to find.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is fairly expensive and somewhat difficult to find. But it is possible. Search for something in the West End if you're going to University of Glasgow.

questions.answer: Courses were not difficult but very interesting. Very easy to pass.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more focus on broader perspectives than narrow legal dogmatism.

questions.answer: Criminal Justice, Contemporary Issues in Healthcare Law, and Roman Law of Property and Obligations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would definitely recommend healthcare law and roman law.

What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to the Highlands, go hiking, and see the nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Scotland is a very welcoming and open country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in the different events in the beginning. That's when you really have to invest in finding social groups. ESN society is a really good option, but also try others.

questions.answer: Invest in the social life. Travel.
